aaron.title: Aaron
aaron.about: High Priest living at the time of Egypt and Wilderness
aaron.note: Moses's older brother, and the one God sent to do the talking when Moses said he could not. He became Israel's first high priest, and the priesthood ran through his sons after him. Most of the time he is standing next to Moses.

abia.title: Abia
abia.about: Man living at the time of Divided Monarchy
abia.note: Luke uses the same spelling for something else entirely: the eighth of the twenty-four priestly rotas, which is the one Zechariah was serving in.

abilene.title: Abilene
abilene.note: A small tetrarchy in the hills between Damascus and Baalbek, named after its main town Abila. Luke puts Lysanias over it when he dates the start of John the Baptist's ministry, and an inscription found near the site, from Tiberius's reign, names a tetrarch called Lysanias.

abraham.title: Abraham
abraham.about: Man living at the time of the Patriarchs
abraham.note: God called him out of Ur and he went at seventy-five, which is most of what you need to know about him. The nation came out of that.

adam.title: Adam
adam.about: Man living at the time before the Flood
adam.note: The first man. The name is the ordinary Hebrew word for man, which is the point of it.

addi.title: Addi
addi.about: Man living at the time of Exile and Return
addi.note: Luke's genealogy has him between Cosam and Melchi, and that is his only appearance.

alpheus.title: Alpheus
alpheus.about: Man living at the time of the New Testament
alpheus.note: Father of the apostle James, which is how that James is told apart from James the son of Zebedee.

aminadab.title: Aminadab
aminadab.about: Man living at the time of Egypt and Wilderness
aminadab.note: Amminadab in its Greek form. Matthew and Luke both name him as David's ancestor through Judah, and his daughter Elisheba married Aaron, so the one family runs into the priests and the kings.

amos-2.title: Amos
amos-2.about: Man living at the time of Exile and Return
amos-2.note: Luke names him once, and he is a man from the exile and the return.

andrew.title: Andrew
andrew.about: Apostle living at the time of the New Testament
andrew.note: Peter's brother, and in John's Gospel a disciple of John the Baptist first, who followed Jesus and straight away brought Peter to meet him. He keeps turning up at practical moments: the boy with five loaves and two fish, the Greeks who came asking for Jesus. Tradition says he was crucified on an X-shaped cross.

anna.title: Anna
anna.about: Woman living at the time of the New Testament
anna.note: An old prophetess of the tribe of Asher. She had been widowed after seven years of marriage and spent decades in the temple praying and fasting. The day Mary and Joseph brought Jesus in, she came up just after Simeon had spoken, and she told others who were waiting for Jerusalem's redemption.

annas.title: Annas
annas.about: High Priest living at the time of the New Testament
annas.note: High priest from AD 6 to 15, put in by the Roman legate Quirinius and removed by the procurator Valerius Gratus. Rome could take the office off him and apparently not the standing: the Gospels still call him high priest next to Caiaphas, who was his son-in-law.

arphaxad.title: Arphaxad
arphaxad.about: Man living at the time of the Patriarchs
arphaxad.note: Shem's son, born two years after the flood. Genesis runs his descendants down through several generations to Abraham, so he is the link between Noah and the patriarchs.

aser.title: Aser
aser.about: Jacob's son living at the time of the Patriarchs
aser.note: The Greek form of Asher, Jacob's eighth son. Luke uses it for the tribe of the prophetess Anna, and Revelation 7:6 lists it among the sealed tribes.

augustus.title: Augustus
augustus.about: Emperor living at the time of the New Testament
augustus.note: The first Roman emperor, under whom Christ was born. His decree that all the world should be taxed is what put the birth in Bethlehem. The name is a title, majesty, first given him by the senate, and later emperors carried it too.

baptist.title: Baptist
baptist.note: John, son of the priest Zechariah and Elizabeth. He was born to elderly parents after an angel said he would be. He preached in the wilderness.

bartholomeus.title: Bartholomeus
bartholomeus.about: Apostle living at the time of the New Testament
bartholomeus.note: One of the twelve. Many take him for Nathanael, since the Synoptic Gospels never mention a Nathanael and John's Gospel never mentions a Bartholomew.

bethlehem.title: Bethlehem
bethlehem.note: House of bread. It is a small town about five miles south of Jerusalem, earlier called Ephrath, where Rachel died and was buried and where Ruth gleaned in Boaz's fields. David was born there and anointed there.

bethsaida.title: Bethsaida
bethsaida.note: A fishing town on the north shore of the Sea of Galilee, home to Peter, Andrew and Philip. Jesus rebuked it more sharply than any of the Galilean towns that would not repent.

boaz.title: Boaz
boaz.note: A wealthy landowner in Bethlehem, related to Naomi's dead husband Elimelech. He noticed Ruth, the widowed Moabite, gleaning behind his harvesters, and he agreed to act as kinsman-redeemer.

caesar-3.title: Caesar
caesar-3.about: Emperor living at the time of the New Testament
caesar-3.note: Luke puts names to the title: Augustus, under whom Jesus was born, and Tiberius after him.

caiaphas.title: Caiaphas
caiaphas.about: High Priest living at the time of the New Testament
caiaphas.note: The high priest who presided over the council that condemned Jesus. Beforehand he argued it was better for one man to die for the people than for the whole nation to suffer, and John's Gospel reads those words as more than he knew.

cainan.title: Cainan
cainan.about: Man living at the time of the Patriarchs
cainan.note: Two men in the genealogies. One descends from Seth several generations before Noah; the other is a son of Arphaxad in Luke's genealogy of Jesus, a name missing from the Genesis Hebrew text but present in the Greek.

capernaum.title: Capernaum
capernaum.note: Jesus left Nazareth and made this fishing town on the northwest shore of the Sea of Galilee his base, and it is called his own city. Several of his best known miracles and teachings happened there.

chorazin.title: Chorazin
chorazin.note: Jesus did many of his miracles in this Galilee town and then pronounced a woe on it, alongside Bethsaida and Capernaum, because it did not repent. It is identified with Khirbet Karazeh about two miles north of Capernaum, where a black basalt synagogue has been dug up.

christ.title: Christ
christ.about: Man living at the time of the New Testament
christ.note: A title, not a surname. It is the Greek for the Hebrew Messiah, the anointed one, and the New Testament gives it to Jesus of Nazareth as the king, priest and deliverer the Old Testament promised. His life and ministry are under Jesus.

chuza.title: Chuza
chuza.about: Man living at the time of the New Testament
chuza.note: Steward of Herod Antipas's household. He is mainly known through his wife Joanna, who had been healed by Jesus, put her own money toward him and the disciples, and was later among the women at the empty tomb.

cosam.title: Cosam
cosam.about: Man living at the time of Divided Monarchy
cosam.note: A name in Luke's genealogy of Jesus, son of Elmodam and father of Addi, and nothing more than that.

david.title: David
david.about: King living at the time of United Monarchy
david.note: The shepherd from Bethlehem who killed Goliath and became Israel's second king, ruling the largest territory Israel ever held, which Solomon then inherited. Solomon was one of his sons. Nearly half the psalms carry his name, and the Tel Dan inscription, where an enemy king boasts over the house of David, put his dynasty outside the Bible as well.

easter.title: Easter
easter.note: The King James has Easter once, at Acts 12:4, and the Greek word underneath it is pascha, Passover. Every later translation says so.

eber.title: Eber
eber.about: Man living at the time of the Patriarchs
eber.note: Several generations before Abraham in Shem's line, and his name is the likely source of the word Hebrew.

eliakim-2.title: Eliakim
eliakim-2.about: Man living at the time of Divided Monarchy
eliakim-2.note: A man from the divided-kingdom years, and Luke is the only book that names him.

eliezer-11.title: Eliezer
eliezer-11.about: Man living at the time of Divided Monarchy
eliezer-11.note: One of 11 men called Eliezer. This one is a man from the divided-kingdom years, named once in Luke.

elijah.title: Elijah
elijah.about: Prophet living at the time of Divided Monarchy
elijah.note: A prophet from Tishbe in Gilead who took on Ahab and Jezebel over Baal worship and beat 450 prophets of Baal on Mount Carmel with fire from heaven. Straight after, he ran into the wilderness sure he was the last faithful man left, and God met him in a quiet voice, not in wind or earthquake or fire. He did not die; a whirlwind took him up while Elisha watched.

elisabeth.title: Elisabeth
elisabeth.note: Elizabeth was old and childless, married to the priest Zechariah, when Gabriel said she would bear a son. When Mary came to visit, the child in Elizabeth's womb leapt. She was the first in the Gospels to call Mary blessed and to see by the Spirit whom Mary was carrying.

elisha.title: Elisha
elisha.about: Prophet living at the time of Divided Monarchy
elisha.note: A farmer's son who was ploughing when Elijah threw his cloak over him. He left the oxen, followed, and asked for a double portion of Elijah's spirit when the older man was taken up. His miracles run from poisoned water made clean to Naaman healed of leprosy, and a dead man thrown into his tomb came back to life when he touched the bones.

elmodam.title: Elmodam
elmodam.about: Man living at the time of Divided Monarchy
elmodam.note: Son of Er in Luke's genealogy of Jesus, in the line that runs back to David's son Nathan.

enoch.title: Enoch
enoch.about: Man living at the time before the Flood
enoch.note: Seventh from Adam. Genesis says he walked with God, and then he was not, for God took him, with no death notice like the others. Jude quotes a prophecy in his name, and a whole later body of Jewish apocalyptic writing carries it too, though written centuries after him.

enos.title: Enos
enos.about: Man living at the time before the Flood
enos.note: Seth's son. In his days, Genesis says, people began to call on the name of the Lord.

er-3.title: Er
er-3.about: Man living at the time of Divided Monarchy
er-3.note: One of 3 men called Er. This one is a man from the divided-kingdom years, named once in Luke.

esli.title: Esli
esli.about: Man living at the time of Exile and Return
esli.note: Son of Naggai and father of Nahum in Luke's genealogy, in the line through Nathan, and nothing else is recorded about him.

esrom.title: Esrom
esrom.about: Man living at the time of Egypt and Wilderness
esrom.note: Hezron, in the Greek form. He was Judah's grandson through Perez and is in both Matthew's and Luke's genealogies of Jesus.

gabriel.title: Gabriel
gabriel.note: Daniel meets him first, explaining the visions of coming empires. In Luke he announces two births, John's to Zechariah and Jesus's to Mary, and tells Zechariah he is the one who stands in the presence of God. He is one of only two angels the Bible names.

galilee.title: Galilee
galilee.note: Jesus grew up here and did most of his public work around the Sea of Galilee. Judeans thought the north provincial and mixed, which is the edge on Nathanael's question about whether anything good could come out of Nazareth.

gennesaret.title: Gennesaret
gennesaret.note: The fertile plain on the northwest shore of the Sea of Galilee, and by extension the lake itself, which the Old Testament calls Chinnereth. Josephus said almost every kind of tree and crop grew there most of the year. In 1986 a first-century fishing boat came out of the mud near Kibbutz Ginosar on that shore.

gergesene.title: Gergesene
gergesene.note: They lived east of the Sea of Galilee, where Jesus sent a legion of demons out of a tormented man and into a herd of pigs that ran into the water and drowned. The same people are also called Gadarenes.

heli.title: Heli
heli.about: Man living at the time of the New Testament
heli.note: Luke 3:23 makes him Joseph's father, where Matthew names Jacob. Readers since antiquity have said Luke is tracing Mary's line, or that a levirate marriage explains it, and the question is still open.

herod-2.title: Herod
herod-2.note: King when Jesus was born. When the magi did not come back to him, Herod the Great ordered the boys of Bethlehem killed. He also enlarged the Jerusalem temple, and Josephus tells his story at length.

herod.title: Herod
herod.about: Tetrarch living at the time of the New Testament
herod.note: Herod Antipas, the son of Herod the Great. He ruled Galilee through Jesus's ministry and beheaded John the Baptist for condemning his marriage, and Luke has him mock Jesus before the crucifixion.

herodias.title: Herodias
herodias.about: Woman living at the time of the New Testament
herodias.note: Granddaughter of Herod the Great. She left her first husband for his half-brother, Herod Antipas, and when John the Baptist called the marriage unlawful she had her daughter dance at a banquet and ask for his head. Josephus gives a different reason for John's death, a political execution.

isaac.title: Isaac
isaac.about: Man living at the time of the Patriarchs
isaac.note: Abraham and Sarah's promised son, born when his father was a hundred. God told Abraham to sacrifice him on Mount Moriah and provided a ram at the last moment. Old and blind, he was tricked by Jacob into giving him Esau's blessing, and he never left Canaan or took a second wife.

isaiah.title: Isaiah
isaiah.about: Prophet living at the time of Divided Monarchy
isaiah.note: Amoz's son, a prophet in Jerusalem in the eighth century, who counselled four kings of Judah and is quoted in the New Testament more than any other prophet. He gave his two sons names that were sermons, Shear-jashub and Maher-shalal-hash-baz. When Sennacherib besieged Jerusalem he told Hezekiah the city would stand, and the Taylor Prism brags of the siege without ever claiming the city fell.

iscariot.title: Iscariot
iscariot.about: Apostle living at the time of the New Testament
iscariot.note: Judas Iscariot kept the money for the twelve, and John says he stole from it. He sold Jesus for thirty pieces of silver and picked him out with a kiss in Gethsemane. Afterwards he gave the money back and hanged himself, though Matthew and Acts tell his death differently.

israel.title: Israel
israel.about: Man living at the time of the Patriarchs
israel.note: God gave Jacob this name after he wrestled through the night at Peniel. It became the name of the nation that came from his twelve sons, and later of the northern kingdom and of the land. For the man himself, see Jacob.

ituraea.title: Ituraea
ituraea.note: Northeast of Galilee, around Mount Hermon and the Anti-Lebanon, and Philip ruled it with Trachonitis when John began preaching. Its people, the Itureans, were semi-nomadic Arabs.

jairus.title: Jairus
jairus.about: Man living at the time of the New Testament
jairus.note: He ran the synagogue at Capernaum, and his twelve-year-old daughter was dying. Jesus was held up on the way, word came that she was dead, and he went to the house anyway and raised her.

james.title: James
james.about: Apostle living at the time of the New Testament
james.note: Zebedee's son and John's older brother. He was one of the three closest to Jesus, and the first of the twelve to be killed, by Herod Agrippa the First.

james-3.title: James
james-3.about: Apostle living at the time of the New Testament
james-3.note: Alphaeus's son, one of the twelve, and the Gospels say almost nothing else about him.

james-4.title: James
james-4.about: Father of an apostle living at the time of the New Testament
james-4.note: A man from the New Testament, named twice across Luke and Acts.

janna.title: Janna
janna.about: Man living at the time of Exile and Return
janna.note: In Luke's genealogy of Jesus, between Joseph and Melchi. Some manuscripts spell it Jannai.

jared.title: Jared
jared.about: Man living at the time before the Flood
jared.note: Enoch's father, in Seth's line down to Noah, and he lived nine hundred sixty-two years.

jericho.title: Jericho
jericho.note: Israel crossed the Jordan and Jericho was the first city it took, walled and gated, with its own king. Achan died for what he stole from the plunder there, a Babylonian robe and silver that belonged to God. By then the place was already ancient: digging at the site has turned up remains about ten thousand years old.

jerusalem.title: Jerusalem
jerusalem.note: David took it from the Jebusites and made it his capital, and once Solomon's temple stood there it was the centre of Israel's worship for a thousand years. Babylon destroyed it, the exiles rebuilt it, Rome destroyed it again in AD 70. Jesus died and rose just outside its walls, and Revelation ends with a new Jerusalem coming down from heaven.

jesse.title: Jesse
jesse.about: David's father living at the time of United Monarchy
jesse.note: Obed's son and Boaz and Ruth's grandson, a man of some standing in Bethlehem with eight sons, the youngest David. Isaiah's "stem of Jesse" is David's family, and the "root of Jesse" is the Messiah. The last we see of him, David is getting him a safe place with the king of Moab.

jesus.title: Jesus
jesus.about: Man living at the time of the New Testament
jesus.note: Born in Bethlehem to Mary and raised in Nazareth in Galilee. Around thirty he began teaching in parables, healing, and gathering twelve disciples, until he was arrested in Jerusalem at Passover, tried before the council and Pontius Pilate, and crucified. His followers said he rose bodily three days later, and the New Testament names him the Messiah, God's own Son become human.

joanna.title: Joanna
joanna.about: Woman living at the time of the New Testament
joanna.note: She was the wife of Chuza, a steward of Herod Antipas, and she helped pay for Jesus' ministry out of her own means. She was also one of the women who found the tomb empty and went to tell the apostles.

joannas.title: Joannas
joannas.about: Man living at the time of Exile and Return
joannas.note: The genealogy in Luke puts him among Zerubbabel's descendants, through Nathan's line, and Matthew leaves him out. Nothing further about him is recorded.

john-2.title: John
john-2.about: Apostle living at the time of the New Testament
john-2.note: Zebedee's son and James's younger brother, a fisherman, and with Peter and James one of the three who saw what the rest did not, the transfiguration and Gethsemane among it. From the cross Jesus gave him his mother Mary to look after. Tradition makes him the disciple Jesus loved and credits him with the fourth Gospel, three letters, and Revelation, written in exile on Patmos.

john.title: John
john.about: Prophet living at the time of the New Testament
john.note: The prophet who comes out of the wilderness in Matthew 3, preaching repentance and baptising. Jesus came to him to be baptised. Later, from prison, he sent his own disciples to ask whether Jesus was the one.

jonan.title: Jonan
jonan.about: Man living at the time of Divided Monarchy
jonan.note: Eliakim's son, in Luke's genealogy of Jesus.

jordan.title: Jordan
jordan.note: It runs from the slopes of Mount Hermon through the Sea of Galilee and down the Rift Valley to the Dead Sea, about sixty five miles in a straight line and nearer two hundred as the river winds. Israel crossed it on dry ground under Joshua, Elijah and Elisha each parted it, and John the Baptist baptised Jesus in it.

jorim.title: Jorim
jorim.about: Man living at the time of Divided Monarchy
jorim.note: Matthat's son, in Luke's genealogy, which follows David's line through Nathan and not Solomon. Nothing else is recorded of him.

jose.title: Jose
jose.about: Man living at the time of Divided Monarchy
jose.note: Eliezer's son. He is one name in Luke's line of Joseph's ancestors through Nathan, and nothing else is known about him.

joseph-8.title: Joseph
joseph-8.about: Man living at the time of Divided Monarchy
joseph-8.note: A man from the divided-kingdom years, and Luke is the only book that names him.

joseph-7.title: Joseph
joseph-7.about: Man living at the time of Exile and Return
joseph-7.note: One of 5 men called Joseph. This one is a man from the exile and the return, named once in Luke.

joseph-2.title: Joseph
joseph-2.about: Mary's husband living at the time of the New Testament
joseph-2.note: A descendant of David from Nazareth, engaged to Mary when she turned out to be pregnant. An angel in a dream talked him out of quietly ending it, and he raised Jesus as his legal father. Scripture says nothing of him after Jesus's boyhood.

juda-h.title: Juda
juda-h.about: -h (Man living at the time of Divided Monarchy
juda-h.note: They named a lot of men Judah. This one sits in Luke 3:30, in Jesus's line of ancestors, generations after the patriarch, and nothing else is said of him.

judaea.title: Judaea
judaea.note: The Roman name for the southern part of the land around Jerusalem, roughly old Judah. Client kings of Herod's family ruled it, then Roman procurators like Pontius Pilate. John the Baptist preached in its wilderness and the Passion happened there. After the revolt of AD 66 to 70 Rome struck coins reading "Judaea Capta."

judah.title: Judah
judah.about: Jacob's son living at the time of the Patriarchs
judah.note: Leah's fourth son, and the brother who ends up leading. He talked the others into selling Joseph rather than killing him, and later offered himself as a hostage in Benjamin's place. His tribe produced David's royal line and gave its name to the southern kingdom, and Jacob's dying blessing promised the sceptre would not leave him.

lamech.title: Lamech
lamech.about: Man living at the time before the Flood
lamech.note: Noah's father, from Seth's line. He named his son Noah in the hope that the boy would bring relief from farming the cursed ground. Luke's genealogy keeps him as one link in the chain.

levi-4.title: Levi
levi-4.about: Apostle living at the time of the New Testament
levi-4.note: The tax collector better known as Matthew. One verse after Jesus called him from his booth, Levi threw a big dinner for him, full of tax collectors and other outcasts, and the Pharisees complained.

levi-3.title: Levi
levi-3.about: Man living at the time of Divided Monarchy
levi-3.note: This is Matthew the tax collector. Mark and Luke call him Levi when they tell the story of his calling.

levi-2.title: Levi
levi-2.about: Man living at the time of Exile and Return
levi-2.note: A Levi in Luke's genealogy, and not Levi the tax collector.

levite.title: Levite
levite.about: Jacob's son living at the time of the Patriarchs
levite.note: They belonged to the tribe of Levi and served at the tabernacle and later the temple, helping the priests, who came from Aaron's branch of the same tribe. Their work was religious, so they got no tribal land, only forty eight towns among the other tribes and the tithes of Israel. Over time they carried and guarded the holy things, sang, kept the gates, and taught the law.

lysanias.title: Lysanias
lysanias.about: Tetrarch of Abilene living at the time of the New Testament
lysanias.note: Tetrarch of Abilene, on the eastern slope of the Anti-Lebanon near Damascus, and one of the rulers Luke uses to date his story. Josephus confirms the tetrarchy was real.

maath.title: Maath
maath.about: Man living at the time of Exile and Return
maath.note: One name in Luke's genealogy of Jesus, between the exile and Joseph.

magdalene.title: Magdalene
magdalene.note: It means "from Magdala," the town on the Sea of Galilee, and it keeps this Mary apart from the other Marys in the Gospels. She watched the crucifixion and was the first to see the risen Jesus. The old idea that she was the sinful woman of Luke 7 has nothing in the text behind it.

mainan.title: Mainan
mainan.about: Man living at the time of Divided Monarchy
mainan.note: A name in Luke's genealogy of Jesus, from David's son Nathan, a few generations above Mattatha and Melea. The Old Testament never mentions him.

maleleel.title: Maleleel
maleleel.about: Man living at the time before the Flood
maleleel.note: Luke's Greek spelling of Mahalalel, Seth's descendant before the flood, in the genealogy that runs back through Noah to Adam.

martha.title: Martha
martha.about: Woman living at the time of the New Testament
martha.note: Lazarus and Mary's sister, at Bethany. Jesus gently told her off for fussing over the meal while Mary sat and listened. Later, grieving her brother, she said one of the boldest things anyone says in the Gospels, that Jesus was the Christ, the Son of God, just before he raised Lazarus.

mary.title: Mary
mary.about: Jesus' mother living at the time of the New Testament
mary.note: Jesus' mother. She was engaged to Joseph when Gabriel told her she would bear the Messiah, she raised Jesus in Nazareth, and she stood at the cross when he died.

mary-2.title: Mary
mary-2.about: Lazarus' sister living at the time of the New Testament
mary-2.note: She sat at Jesus' feet listening while Martha did the work. This is the Mary of Bethany, sister of Martha and Lazarus, who not long before his death anointed his feet with expensive perfume.

mathat-2.title: Mathat
mathat-2.about: Man living at the time of Divided Monarchy
mathat-2.note: Luke's genealogy has two men called Mathat, and this is the one further back, near Levi.

mathat.title: Mathat
mathat.about: Man living at the time of Exile and Return
mathat.note: Luke's genealogy of Joseph has two men called Mathat, one near Joseph's own generation and one much further back near Levi and Melki. Little is known of either.

mattatha.title: Mattatha
mattatha.about: Man living at the time of United Monarchy
mattatha.note: Nathan's son and David's grandson in Luke's genealogy, which runs Jesus' line through Nathan instead of Solomon.

mattathias.title: Mattathias
mattathias.about: Man living at the time of Exile and Return
mattathias.note: Two of them stand next to each other in Luke's genealogy, the son of Amos and the son of Semein, both some generations above Joseph. Neither is known otherwise. The priest who started the Maccabean revolt carried the same name, but he is a different man.

mattathias-2.title: Mattathias
mattathias-2.about: Man living at the time of Exile and Return
mattathias-2.note: Luke's genealogy has two of them in consecutive generations, and neither is mentioned anywhere else.

matthew.title: Matthew
matthew.about: Apostle living at the time of the New Testament
matthew.note: A tax collector, which made him an outcast among fellow Jews for working on Rome's behalf, until Jesus called him straight from his booth to be one of the twelve. Mark and Luke call him Levi. He threw a big dinner for Jesus with other tax collectors, and early church tradition says he wrote the Gospel that carries his name, aimed at Jewish readers.

matthew-2.title: Matthew
matthew-2.about: Apostle living at the time of the New Testament
matthew-2.note: Mark and Luke name him twice, and he is a man from the New Testament.

melchi-2.title: Melchi
melchi-2.about: Man living at the time of Divided Monarchy
melchi-2.note: Luke's genealogy has two men of the name, and this is the one further back, near Levi.

melchi.title: Melchi
melchi.about: Man living at the time of Exile and Return
melchi.note: Two ancestors in Luke's genealogy share the name. One fathered Neri around the time of the Babylonian exile; the other, Janna's son and Levi's father, stands much closer to Jesus.

meleas.title: Meleas
meleas.about: Man living at the time of Divided Monarchy
meleas.note: A name in Luke's line through David's son Nathan, between Menan and Eliakim. Nothing else is known of him.

methuselah.title: Methuselah
methuselah.about: Man living at the time before the Flood
methuselah.note: Enoch's son and Noah's grandfather. Genesis gives him nine hundred sixty-nine years, longer than anyone else in the Bible. By the numbers in Genesis 5 he dies the year of the flood, though the text never connects the two. A Book of Noah fragment has him travel to find Enoch when his newborn grandson does not look human.

moses.title: Moses
moses.about: Levite living at the time of Egypt and Wilderness
moses.note: Born a Hebrew slave in Egypt and raised in Pharaoh's house, he killed an Egyptian overseer and ran to Midian, where he kept sheep for forty years. God called him back from the burning bush to face Pharaoh and lead Israel out. He gave them the law at Sinai, led them forty years in the wilderness, and died at a hundred and twenty within sight of the promised land.

naaman.title: Naaman
naaman.about: Syrian living at the time of Divided Monarchy
naaman.note: Commander of the Aramean army, a great man, and a leper. A captured Israelite girl told his household about a prophet in Samaria. Elisha did not even come out, only sent word to wash seven times in the Jordan, and Naaman almost went home angry before his servants talked him round. He came out of the water clean, and Gehazi, who ran after him for a payment, got his leprosy.

naasson.title: Naasson
naasson.note: The Greek spelling of Nahshon, prince of Judah in the wilderness and brother-in-law to Aaron through his sister Elisheba. Matthew and Luke both list him among Jesus' ancestors.

nachor.title: Nachor
nachor.about: Man living at the time of the Patriarchs
nachor.note: Luke's Greek spelling of Nahor, Abraham's grandfather.

nagge.title: Nagge
nagge.about: Man living at the time of Exile and Return
nagge.note: In Luke's genealogy, Maath's son and the father of Esli. Nothing else is known.

nain.title: Nain
nain.note: Jesus met a funeral coming out of this village in Galilee and raised a widow's only son. It sits at the foot of the hill of Moreh and survives as the Arab village of Nein, a few miles southeast of Nazareth.

nathan-2.title: Nathan
nathan-2.about: David's son living at the time of United Monarchy
nathan-2.note: One of David's sons born in Jerusalem. Luke traces Jesus' line through him, not through Solomon.

naum.title: Naum
naum.about: Man living at the time of Exile and Return
naum.note: The Greek form of Nahum, a name in Luke's genealogy, son of Esli and father of Amos. Luke's line after David runs through Nathan, which is why it parts from Matthew's.

nazareth.title: Nazareth
nazareth.note: A small village in the hills of Galilee, never named in the Old Testament and not thought much of, which is likely the edge on Nathanael's question about whether anything good could come from it. Gabriel came to Mary there, and Jesus grew up there. When he preached in its synagogue, his neighbours drove him out.

neri.title: Neri
neri.about: Man living at the time of Exile and Return
neri.note: Shealtiel's father in Luke's genealogy, on the line through David's son Nathan.

noah.title: Noah
noah.about: Flood survivor living at the time before the Flood
noah.note: God picked him as the one righteous man of his generation and told him to build an ark. His family came through the flood with him, along with pairs of every kind of animal. Afterward God made a covenant with him.

peter.title: Peter
peter.about: Apostle living at the time of the New Testament
peter.note: A Galilean fisherman named Simon. Jesus renamed him Cephas, or Peter, which means rock. He became the most prominent of the twelve, and in Matthew it is his confession that Jesus is the Messiah the Gospel turns on.

phalec.title: Phalec
phalec.about: Man living at the time of the Patriarchs
phalec.note: Luke's Greek spelling of Peleg, in the genealogy of Jesus. The Hebrew name means division, and Genesis 10:25 says the earth was divided in his days.

phanuel.title: Phanuel
phanuel.about: Man living at the time of the New Testament
phanuel.note: He is named only to show that Anna, the old prophetess who knew the infant Jesus in the temple, came from the tribe of Asher.

phares.title: Phares
phares.about: Man living at the time of Egypt and Wilderness
phares.note: Matthew and Luke both list Perez, son of Judah and Tamar, in the genealogy of Jesus under this Greek spelling.

pharisee.title: Pharisee
pharisee.about: Religious group in the New Testament
pharisee.note: A Jewish movement devoted to strict keeping of the law, the written text and a large body of oral tradition around it. They carried real weight in the religious life of the people. They argue with Jesus again and again.

philip.title: Philip
philip.about: Apostle living at the time of the New Testament
philip.note: One of the twelve, from Bethsaida like Peter and Andrew. Philip found Nathanael and brought him to Jesus, and in John's Gospel he gets asked how they were going to feed the crowd.

philip-4.title: Philip
philip-4.about: Tetrarch living at the time of the New Testament
philip-4.note: The tetrarch, one of Herod the Great's sons. Luke dates John's ministry by his rule, and Josephus credits him with building Paneas and renaming it Caesarea.

pilate.title: Pilate
pilate.about: Ruler living at the time of the New Testament
pilate.note: Pontius Pilate, Roman governor of Judea. He said three times that he found no guilt in Jesus, and then gave the crowd and the religious leaders what they wanted and had him crucified.

pontius.title: Pontius
pontius.about: Ruler living at the time of the New Testament
pontius.note: Pilate's family name, and the reader wants the entry for Pilate.

quirinius.title: Quirinius
quirinius.about: Man living at the time of the New Testament
quirinius.note: Luke names him once, for the census that takes Joseph and Mary to Bethlehem, and the old spelling is Cyrenius. Josephus opens a book of his history with the same man arriving in Syria to take that kind of account.

ragau.title: Ragau
ragau.about: Man living at the time of the Patriarchs
ragau.note: Reu, son of Peleg, in his Greek spelling in Luke's genealogy of Jesus.

rhesa.title: Rhesa
rhesa.about: Man living at the time of Exile and Return
rhesa.note: Luke lists him as a son of Zerubbabel. Some scholars think the name is really the Aramaic title "resh," meaning prince or head, and was once attached to Zerubbabel himself.

sala.title: Sala
sala.note: Luke's spelling of Shelah, in the genealogy of Jesus between Arphaxad and Abraham.

salathiel-2.title: Salathiel
salathiel-2.about: Man living at the time of Exile and Return
salathiel-2.note: Also spelled Shealtiel. He is Jeconiah's son and Zerubbabel's father, or his uncle, depending which genealogy you follow.

samaritan.title: Samaritan
samaritan.note: The people who lived in Samaria in Jesus' day. 2 Kings traces them back to the Israelites left behind and the foreigners Assyria brought in. They worshiped at a temple of their own.

sarepta.title: Sarepta
sarepta.note: Luke's Greek spelling of Zarephath, a Phoenician town between Tyre and Sidon. Elijah lodged there with a widow and kept her flour and oil from running out. Later he brought her son back to life.

saruch.title: Saruch
saruch.about: Man living at the time of the Patriarchs
saruch.note: Serug, as Luke spells it. Son of Reu and an ancestor of Abraham, he is one of the names in Luke's genealogy of Jesus.

satan.title: Satan
satan.about: An angel in the Old Testament
satan.note: The name means adversary. In Job he questions whether Job's goodness is real, and in Zechariah he stands to accuse Joshua the high priest before the angel of the Lord.

semei.title: Semei
semei.about: Man living at the time of Exile and Return
semei.note: Luke 3:26 has his name in the genealogy of Jesus, and nothing else is known about him.

seth.title: Seth
seth.about: Man living at the time before the Flood
seth.note: After Cain killed Abel, Eve had a third son. She named him Seth, saying God had given her another child in Abel's place. His line is the one Genesis follows forward.

shem.title: Shem
shem.about: Man living at the time of the Patriarchs
shem.note: Noah's oldest son. The Semitic peoples, Abraham's line among them, all trace back to him, and Genesis 10 follows his descendants down to Eber.

sidon.title: Sidon
sidon.note: The older of the two great Phoenician ports, north of Tyre. It was allotted to Asher, but Asher never took it.

simeon-4.title: Simeon
simeon-4.about: Man living at the time of Divided Monarchy
simeon-4.note: One of 4 men called Simeon. This one is a man from the divided-kingdom years, named once in Luke.

simeon-2.title: Simeon
simeon-2.about: Man living at the time of the New Testament
simeon-2.note: Luke names him twice, and he is a man from the New Testament.

simon-4.title: Simon
simon-4.about: Apostle living at the time of the New Testament
simon-4.note: One of the twelve apostles. The title Zealot tells him apart from Simon Peter and probably means he had belonged to a movement opposed to Roman rule. Nothing else about him is recorded.

simon.title: Simon
simon.about: Man living at the time of the New Testament
simon.note: Simon Peter, called from his fishing in Matthew 4:18 and named first among the twelve apostles. In Matthew 16:16 he is the one who answers the question.

sodom.title: Sodom
sodom.note: Sodom was destroyed by fire from heaven along with Gomorrah, and the rest of Scripture keeps pointing back to it as the picture of judgment. It was one of the cities of the plain near the Dead Sea.

susanna.title: Susanna
susanna.about: Woman living at the time of the New Testament
susanna.note: She traveled with Jesus and the twelve and paid toward their keep out of her own means, named in Luke 8:3 next to Mary Magdalene and Joanna. Nothing more is recorded about her.

syria.title: Syria
syria.note: The region northeast of Israel, called Aram in the Old Testament. In the New Testament Antioch was its chief city and the base Paul's journeys started from, and Luke dates Jesus's birth by a census under Quirinius.

syrian.title: Syrian
syrian.note: The Arameans, the people around Damascus, mostly in the wars of the kings in 2 Kings.

terah.title: Terah
terah.about: Man living at the time of the Patriarchs
terah.note: Abraham's father, named once in Luke's genealogy. Josephus tried to give him a date, 292 years after the flood.

theophilus.title: Theophilus
theophilus.about: Man living at the time of the New Testament
theophilus.note: Luke wrote both his Gospel and Acts to him. He calls him most excellent, the title he also uses for Felix and Festus, and that is all anyone knows.

thomas.title: Thomas
thomas.about: Apostle living at the time of the New Testament
thomas.note: One of the twelve, called the twin. He would not believe Jesus had risen until he could touch the wounds, and when Jesus showed him his hands and side he said, my Lord and my God.

tiberius.title: Tiberius
tiberius.about: Emperor living at the time of the New Testament
tiberius.note: The second Roman emperor, after Augustus, from AD 14 to 37. Luke dates the start of John's ministry to the fifteenth year of his reign, in the same verse that names Pilate and Herod.

trachonitis.title: Trachonitis
trachonitis.note: The rugged region, a lava field east of the Sea of Galilee. Philip the tetrarch governed it in the year Luke uses to date John the Baptist. Bandits hid in that ground in Herod's day, and it is still called the Lejah.

tyre.title: Tyre
tyre.note: The leading Phoenician port, partly on the mainland and partly on an island offshore, rich from sea trade and purple dye made from murex shells. Its king Hiram sent cedar and craftsmen for David and Solomon. The prophets attacked its pride and said it would fall.

zebedee.title: Zebedee
zebedee.about: Man living at the time of the New Testament
zebedee.note: He fished, and he was the father of James and John. He had hired men working with him, and when his sons left the boat to follow Jesus, he stayed.

zechariah.title: Zechariah
zechariah.about: Man living at the time of the New Testament
zechariah.note: John the Baptist's father, a priest, and Luke's Gospel opens with him. He is not the Zechariah Jesus mentions later, killed between the altar and the house of God.

zelotes.title: Zelotes
zelotes.about: Apostle living at the time of the New Testament
zelotes.note: The Zealot, Luke's way of telling Simon the apostle from Simon Peter, and Matthew and Mark call him Simon the Canaanite, which means the same thing.

zerubbabel-2.title: Zerubbabel
zerubbabel-2.about: Man living at the time of Exile and Return
zerubbabel-2.note: Luke's genealogy has him at 3:27, between the exile and the more familiar names. He is the governor who rebuilt the temple.
